thread:
sara: FYI ran into a weird one during the GPU job rollout — job failed with 403 from the deploy controller and audit logs show no KMS envelope or decrypt event. wondering if RBAC or audit policy is swallowing KMS events.

kenji: Oof. Which pool / controller?

sara: gpu-pool-prod1, controller is gpu-scheduler v2.1. Error was `deploy-controller: request denied: decrypt denied`. The audit entry only shows the API call, not the KMS envelope id or kms:Decrypt.

ajohnson: That's bad for forensics. We should always surface envelope_id in audit when decrypt is called (redact keys). Might be auditpolicy not capturing system:serviceaccount events for kms.

lisa: Can you paste the raw audit snippet?

sara: Paste below (sanitized):
```
{"kind":"Event","verb":"create","user":{"username":"system:serviceaccount:infra:gpu-scheduler"},"objectRef":{"resource":"jobs","name":"train-2026-03-20"},"responseStatus":{"code":403},"annotations":{}}
```
No kms fields at all.

kenji: Looks like audit policy's `metadata` level set to `Request` for the `secrets`/`configmaps` group, so the api-server is dropping the object details. KMS decrypts happen in our controller code, not the API server, so we need the controller to emit structured audit logs or ensure the apiserver captures the SA identity with `RequestResponse`.

ajohnson: Proposal: 1) update apiserver auditpolicy to RequestResponse for `secrets` & `pods` in infra namespace; 2) add an internal structured audit event in gpu-scheduler that logs `kms:Decrypt` with envelope_id and keyring (envelope_id should be hashed before logging). 3) short RBAC tweak: allow gpu-scheduler SA `get` on `secrets/kms-envelope-id` only.

sara: +1 on hashing envelope_id. We should avoid plaintext envelope ids but need stable trace token. Use HMAC with rotation key stored in vault.

lisa: How risky is the RBAC change? Anyone could escalate if we grant `get` broadly.

kenji: Minimal surface: create a ClusterRole `gpu-scheduler-kms-read` bound to `system:serviceaccount:infra:gpu-scheduler` with `resources: [secrets] verbs: [get] resourceNames: [gpu-kms-envelopes]` and namespace-scoped RoleBinding. No wildcard.

ajohnson: Also we need to update our rollout playbook: feature-flag the structured audit in gpu-scheduler behind `ENABLE_AUDIT_V2`, canary to dev/prod-slice, verify hashed envelope id appears in central logs (elk) and matches job IDs.

sara: Tests: unit test for HMAC hash function, e2e test simulating decrypt flow that asserts an `audit.kms.decrypt` event with `envelope_hash`. Also update SOC runbook to search for envelope_hash and not raw id.

lisa: Who owns the apiserver auditpolicy update? That's a k8s infra change and will bump events.

kenji: I'll own the apiserver change but need approval from platform and SRE. I'll open an RFC and PR with diff of auditpolicy. Plan: set RequestResponse for these rules, monitor EPS and retention. Rollback knob if EPS > threshold.

ajohnson: One more: our log scrubbing lambda needs to be updated to detect and redact raw envelope ids in any accidental free-text logs thrown by 3rd-party libs. But if we switch to hashed envelope ids everywhere, that reduces risk.

sara: Action items: @kenji open PR for auditpolicy (+ perf guardrails) by EOD tomorrow; @ajohnson add structured audit event + feature flag to gpu-scheduler PR by end of week; @lisa add e2e test and update SOC playbook; I'll draft the clusterrole ResourceNames req and a short justification for least-priv review.

kenji: ack. opening PR now and tagging SRE + platform.

auditbot: Incident digest created: `INC-2026-03-gpu-decrypt-403` — added sprints and owners.

lisa: Thanks team. If anyone hits other missing kms events, ping me directly so we can accelerate triage. :+1:
